title: Firebase Performance Monitoring
objectives: Understand Performance Monitoring via a real-life analogy
Read auto-collected app-start, screen-render, network traces
Design custom traces + attributes for business flows
Pick top-line SLIs and alert on regressions
Correlate Perf + Analytics + Crashlytics for release quality

sections.markdown:
**Think of Performance Monitoring as your app's fitness tracker.**

A fitness watch doesn't just say 'you feel tired.' It measures **specific metrics** — resting heart rate, HRV, VO2 max, sleep score — over time, and screams at you when they regress week over week.

Firebase Perf does exactly this for your app:

- **Auto-collected vitals** — cold-start p95, screen-render p95, network-request p95 per endpoint. You don't lift a finger.
- **Custom traces** — you decide what to time (`checkout`, `feed_load`, `pdf_render`) with attributes (`payment_method`, `tenant`, `user_plan`) and metrics (`items_in_cart`).
- **Percentiles, not averages** — p50 hides the pain; **p95 / p99 tell you what your slowest users experience**.
- **Alerts on regression** — 'checkout p95 up 30% since release 2.5.0? Page the on-call.' Same as a fitness watch alerting on abnormal resting heart rate.
- **Slice by app version + device tier + country** — the aggregate can hide a disaster on cheap Android in India.

**Why every mobile team wires this on day one:** without it, 'the app feels slow' is folklore. With it, 'checkout p95 on 2.5.0 is 4.2s vs 3.1s on 2.4.9 for Android 12 users' is a fact. Blocks bad releases before they scale.

**Firebase Performance Monitoring** auto-collects **app-start (cold/warm/hot), foreground/background transitions, screen render (slow-frames / frozen-frames), and HTTP/S network request timings**. Adds an SDK for **custom traces** (any code region) + **screen traces** (frame timings per screen). Ships percentile aggregates + attribute breakdowns to a Firebase console dashboard; also feeds BigQuery. Free at any volume. Sampling is automatic; there's a per-project session cap.

## Custom trace patterns

**Rule: time flows that matter to users or revenue.** Not every code path.

- **`app_start` (auto)** — reference baseline.
- **`first_meaningful_paint`** — first frame with real data (post-hydration).
- **`feed_load`** — pull-to-refresh flow.
- **`checkout`** — cart-review to payment-success.
- **`upload_photo`** — pick + compress + upload.
- **`pdf_render`** — page-1 render for a document.
- **`report_generate`** — expensive local computation.

**Attributes** (max 5 per trace): `tenant`, `payment_method`, `variant` (RC), `network` (wifi/cellular), `screen`.

**Metrics** (max 32 per trace, numeric): `items_in_cart`, `bytes_transferred`, `retry_count`.
## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Instrumenting everything.** Every function timed = noise, no signal, no clear SLO. Time 2-5 top business flows, no more.
**Mistake 2: Watching averages, not p95/p99.** `avg=1.2s` hides the 5% of users at 8s. Alert on p95 regression, not mean.
**Mistake 3: Not slicing by attributes.** Aggregate p95 fine; but Android 12 + Redmi p95 disaster. Slice by device tier, OS, country, tenant.
**Mistake 4: No release-over-release comparison.** Release 2.5.0 dashboard alone tells you nothing without 2.4.9 baseline.
**Mistake 5: Trace overlap / leaked traces.** `start` without `stop` = phantom hangs. Always `try/finally` around the flow.
**Mistake 6: PII in attributes.** Never `user_email` as an attribute. Only pseudonymous fields (`plan`, `tenant`).
**Mistake 7: Ignoring network traces.** Auto-collected but often ignored — where most 'app slow' complaints actually come from. Set an alert on `api.example.com p95 > 2s`.
**Mistake 8: Not disabling in DEBUG.** Debug builds bloat aggregate p95 (hot-reload spikes, debugger pauses).
## Best practices
**1. Define 3-5 top-line SLIs.** Cold-start p95, checkout p95, feed_load p95, key API p95, screen render slow-frames %. Everything else is diagnostic.
**2. Alert on release-over-release regression** — > 15-20% p95 change = automatic bug bug.
**3. Slice by device tier + country + variant** — hidden failures live here.
**4. Attributes for business context** — `payment_method`, `tenant`, `remote_config_variant`, `network`.
**5. HTTP metrics for outbound network** — every critical API endpoint measured.
**6. Try/finally around every trace** — no phantom hangs.
**7. Respect telemetry consent** — `setPerformanceCollectionEnabled` gated by user choice.
**8. Correlate with Crashlytics + Analytics** — same UID, same custom keys — story of a slow release.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy) — Turn on Perf.** Wire SDK; verify `app_start` + auto network appear in the console after a session.
**Practice 2 (Medium) — Custom trace.** Wrap `checkout` with attributes (`payment_method`, `tenant`) + a metric (`items_in_cart`).
**Practice 3 (Medium) — HTTP metric.** Manually measure a Dio request; compare against auto-collected trace.
**Practice 4 (Hard) — SLI alerting.** Define cold-start p95 + checkout p95 alerts; simulate regression + verify alert fires.
**Practice 5 (Hard) — Slice by device tier.** Break out Redmi Note 9 users specifically; verify p95 differs; discuss.
**Practice 6 (Expert) — Release-gate.** CI pipeline blocks promotion to prod if p95 for cold-start or checkout regresses > 20% vs previous release.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: What does Firebase Performance auto-collect and what do you have to add manually?**

**A:** **Auto:** cold-start / warm-start / hot-start durations, foreground/background transitions, per-screen slow-frames + frozen-frames rates (via screen traces), and HTTP/S request timings (URL, status, response size, duration) — the SDK swizzles the HTTP client to capture these transparently. **Manual:** **custom traces** for any business flow (`checkout`, `feed_load`, `pdf_render`) via `newTrace('name').start() / stop()`; **HTTP metrics** for requests not caught by auto-instrumentation (some custom Dio interceptors bypass it); **attributes** (up to 5 string attributes per trace) for slicing; **metrics** (up to 32 numeric metrics per trace) for aggregating (`items_in_cart`, `bytes_transferred`, `retry_count`). **Key rule:** don't trace everything — 2-5 top-line flows. Aggregate p95 in the console, alert on release-over-release regression. **Also NOT auto:** Flutter widget-tree render timings; there's a `withPerformanceOverlay` for local dev, and newer plugin versions provide a navigator observer for auto screen traces.

**Q2: Averages vs percentiles — why does Firebase Perf show p50/p75/p90/p95?**

**A:** Latency distributions are **long-tailed** — a few users experience durations 10-50x the median. **Averages hide this** — if 95 users take 0.5s and 5 users take 10s, mean = 0.975s. Sounds fine. But 5% of users are miserable. **Percentiles reveal tails:** p50 = median (typical user), p95 = the 95th-worst user (a slow user), p99 = the very slowest 1%. **Firebase surfaces p50/p75/p90/p95** for exactly this reason. **SLO on p95** — 'checkout p95 < 3s for Tier-2 Android devices' — because that's what your slowest realistic users hit. **Alerts fire on p95 regressions** — 'p95 up 30% since 2.5.0' — because a bad release can silently move only the tail. **Averages are OK for anomaly *detection*, useless for target-setting.**

**Q3: Which SLIs would you alert on for a Flutter app? Give a concrete SLO.**

**A:** **Top-line SLIs:** **(1) app_start_cold p95** — target ≤ 2.5s p95 on median device. **(2) `checkout` custom trace p95** — ≤ 3s. **(3) `feed_load` custom trace p95** — ≤ 1.5s. **(4) HTTP metric `POST /orders` p95** — ≤ 800ms. **(5) Screen trace `HomeScreen` slow-frames %** — ≤ 5%; frozen-frames % ≤ 0.5%. **Alerts:** any of (1-4) regressing > 20% release-over-release fires PagerDuty. Any of (5) slipping beyond target for a full day fires Slack. **Slice by** app version, device tier (via device model → tier lookup), country, RC variant. **Combine with Crashlytics + Analytics conversion drop** — a slow AND crashy release is bad; either one alone is worth investigating. **Release-gate** the CI pipeline: block promotion to prod if any SLI regressed > 20% in the 24h internal-QA window.

**Q4: How do you use custom traces effectively — what are the do's and don'ts?**

**A:** **Do:** (1) **Wrap business-critical flows** — check-out, feed-load, first-meaningful-paint. (2) **`try/finally` around `stop()`** — otherwise a thrown exception = phantom hang skewing p95. (3) **Attributes for high-cardinality slicing** — `payment_method`, `tenant`, `remote_config_variant`, `network`. Max 5 string attributes per trace. (4) **Metrics for numeric aggregation** — `items_in_cart`, `bytes_transferred`. Max 32 numeric metrics. (5) **Consistent naming** across versions — Firebase groups by name. **Don't:** (1) Time every function — noise. (2) Overlap traces of the same name in the same session — the SDK stops both when either stops. (3) Attach PII as attributes — pseudonymous only. (4) Use dynamic values in NAMES (e.g., `checkout_<user_id>`) — explodes the trace-name cardinality; there's a cap. (5) Time inside `build()` — Perf overhead + you can't guarantee `stop`.

**Q5: How do you correlate Perf + Crashlytics + Analytics to explain a bad release?**

**A:** Story-of-a-release: **(1)** Analytics conversion drops by 15% after 2.5.0 rollout. **(2)** Crashlytics shows a modest crash-free-users % drop from 99.6 → 99.3% — not catastrophic. **(3)** Perf shows checkout p95 up 40% for Android 12. **(4) Slice by RC variant** — Perf p95 regression is concentrated in `checkout_layout_version=3`. Analytics conversion drop is in the same segment. **Hypothesis:** the new checkout layout is slow, users abandon, small crash bump is from timeout retries. **(5)** Flip RC variant back to `version=2` for the affected cohort → watch p95 recover in 24h → confirm hypothesis → hotfix + re-release. **This cross-service triage** is where every senior interview goes — the ability to weave 3 signals into 1 explanation. Same UID + custom keys (`variant`, `tenant`, `payment_method`) across all three services is what enables it. BigQuery export unifies + lets you SQL against the combined dataset.

**Q6: Perf overhead + sampling — what should you know?**

**A:** Firebase Perf is **low-overhead by design** (< 1% CPU + memory typically) but has **automatic sampling** — the SDK doesn't collect every session's traces, only a subset chosen to keep console volumes manageable. **Sampling rate** is controlled per-project (backend) + can be tuned via `setPerformanceCollectionEnabled` on the client (all or nothing per client). **You don't manually decide 'sample this trace'** — the SDK handles it. **Implication:** p95 in the console is a **statistical estimate**, not exact. For heavy-tail investigations, cross-check via BigQuery export. **Overhead sources:** HTTP-client instrumentation (swizzling), foreground/background listeners, on-disk queue of unsent events, network flush every N minutes. **Turn OFF in tests** — CI benchmark suites shouldn't include Perf. **Turn OFF in some Dart isolates** — the SDK is main-isolate only; background isolate init is a no-op.

## Real-world usage

- **Every serious mobile team** — 3-5 SLIs monitored, release gates.
- **Startup optimization** — cold start reductions are a shipped-quarterly-goal at most consumer apps.
- **Backend SLO signal** — 'our mobile p95 for /orders is 2s; backend claims 400ms — network is the bottleneck.'
- **A/B test measurement** — RC variant A vs B on p95 tells you if a new layout is slower.
- **Not a replacement for** — Sentry Performance (deeper distributed traces via OTel), Firebase Test Lab (device farm), macrobenchmark (Android profiling).
- **BigQuery integration** — join Perf events with Crashlytics + Analytics for one 'session story.'

## Advanced notes

- **BigQuery export** — every trace event + attributes + metrics → SQL-queryable, unlimited retention.
- **Auto screen traces (Flutter)** — newer plugin versions provide a `PerformanceObserver` for `MaterialApp.navigatorObservers`.
- **Screen-trace metrics** — slow-frames %, frozen-frames %, total-frames — jank UX SLO.
- **HTTP URL patterning** — Firebase groups similar URLs (`/orders/{id}` → one bucket); avoid trailing IDs blowing cardinality.
- **Web Vitals for Web** — LCP, FID, CLS available in Web SDK.
- **Custom-trace name cardinality cap** — ~200 unique names per project. Don't inject dynamic values.
- **`setCollectionEnabled(false)`** — global kill for privacy compliance.
- **DebugView** — real-time trace stream for the connected device — useful in dev.
- **Integration with Google Cloud Trace** — for backend correlation via headers.
- **OpenTelemetry gap** — Perf doesn't emit OTel spans; roll Sentry Perf or Datadog RUM for distributed traces.
- **Anomaly detection** — Firebase Alerts on p95 regression > X% between two releases.
- **Release-gate** — CI pipeline checks the previous 24h p95 for cold-start + checkout; block promotion on regression.
